entities.name: PMID:25089378
observations: In rat R3/1 and L2 and human A549 alveolar epithelial cells, hyperoxia (60–90% O2) reduced LAT1 expression, LAT-system transport, S-nitrosothiol accumulation, and soluble guanylyl cyclase activation after NO treatment; effects increased with exposure duration. Newborn rats exposed to 60% O2 for 4 days also showed reduced lung LAT1 immunostaining.
Evidence implicates LAT1 functionally, but retrieved evidence does not show SLC7A5-specific genetic perturbation or rescue proving sole/necessary causation.

entities.name: PMID:18441097
observations: In rat alveolar epithelial cells, NO-derived S-nitrosothiol species entered after L-cysteine S-nitrosation followed by LAT-mediated uptake; LAT competitors inhibited uptake. This study did not test hyperoxia.

entities.name: PMID:9530177
observations: In human A549 cells, 95% oxygen plus chemically generated NO caused synergistic accelerated cell death and increased nitrotyrosine markers; LAT1 was not measured, so this does not establish LAT1 mediation.

entities.name: Hyperoxia reduces NO signaling
observations: Direct alveolar epithelial cell study found hyperoxia reduced LAT1 expression/transport alongside exogenous-NO-associated S-nitrosothiol accumulation and soluble guanylyl cyclase activation; LAT1 mediation is implicated, but genetic causality is not established in the retrieved evidence.
